text:
anya: heads up — during orion-v3 int8 bringup we saw a reproducible seg/tokenization issue for Chinese date numerals (e.g., 2023年12月25日) that causes downstream translation truncation and BLEU drops.

sam: ugh, repro steps? logs?

anya: repro dataset: internal/date-parsing-cjk, run on orion-v3-quant-int8 vs fp16. Quick sample outputs: 
- fp16: "2023年12月25日" -> kept as single token sequence, correct translation
- int8: "2023 年12 月25 日" -> splits inside year/month markers, leads to mistranslation and date reorder

lee: can you paste the tokenized ids?

anya: sure, small snippet: 
```
# fp16 tokens: [3421, 9876, 123, 4567]
# int8 tokens: [3421, 11, 9876, 22, 123, 33, 4567]
```

maria: interesting — looks like ZWSP/zero-width normalization or punctuation category mapping changed after quantized kernel selection. Did we change tokenizer rules on bringup?

anya: tokenizer config is unchanged. suspect tokenization downstream of kernel numeric handling: eval-bot ran a quick smoke across 2k samples: 
```
eval-bot: orion-v3 int8 smoke: date-parsing-cjk: BLEU -3.2 vs fp16, date-accuracy -18% (fp16 96% -> int8 78%)
qa-bot: flagged 124 samples as critical date-misformat
```

sam: ok let's bisect — is this quantization-only? try running the same tokenizer and detok in python with the quantized model weights disabled (i.e., only tokenization step).

anya: ran that already: tokenizer-only local runs (same vocab file) reproduce only when running through the model inference path (so KV cache / kernel path likely influences token boundary emission).

lee: could be prefix cache flushing or attention kernel rounding that changes logits at boundaries for numerals. small prob mass shifts might make model prefer a boundary token.

maria: any reproducible prompt to trigger? code snippet we can use to test quickly?

anya: yes, use this minimal test: 
```
prompt = "今天是2023年12月25日，会议在下午。"
# run through orion-v3-fp16 and orion-v3-int8, compare tokenized detok outputs and translation.
```

sam: quick mitigation idea — add a detok post-rule that merges adjacent numeric+unit tokens for years/months/days if they appear split. Not ideal but buy time for root cause.

lee: agreed. I can patch a lightweight post-detok rule: regex merge for (\d{2,4})\s*年 and 月 日 combos. I'll put a PR.

maria: also create a reproducer that logs logits around the split boundary. we need to see whether the model emits the boundary token or tokenizer's decode differs.

anya: doing that now. logging snippet returns softmax logits for token ids around bytes: 
```
# sample logits around token idx 9876
... 0.11, 0.09, 0.02, 0.35, 0.43 ...
# small shifts make token 11 (ZWSP surrogate) win in int8 runs
```

sam: file an issue with the attach logs and mark P1 if customer-facing. add regression label and tag orion-v3-int8 on it.

anya: filed: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/7891 — includes sample audio/text, eval-bot artifacts, and reproduction script.

lee: PR draft ready: fixes/post-detok-cjk-date-merge. Quick smoke on staging?

maria: please run smoke with eval-bot hook: `eval-bot --suite date-parsing-cjk --model orion-v3-int8 --postfix patch-merge` and report BLEU/date-accuracy.

eval-bot: queued job 4872. estimated 12m.

(12m later)

eval-bot: job 4872 complete: orion-v3-int8 + post-detok patch -> BLEU -0.8 vs fp16, date-accuracy 93% (was 78%). Regression reduced but not fully resolved.

sam: good improvement. keep the patch while we root cause kernel-level behavior. Lee, pair with infra to run kernel-level profiling.

lee: will do. starting with attention kernel differences across cuda/rocm branches. cc @maria for QA regression harness.

maria: QA will run extended suite (10k examples) and monitor any false merges from the post-detok rule. we need to ensure we don't accidentally merge legitimate spaced numerals.

anya: thanks team. I'll update the issue and notify the customer contact. :thumbsup:
